key_results: Sequential U-Net with transfer learning recovers high-quality PFM images from fast-acquired low-quality data; >50% improvement vs random initialization on ferroelectric ceramics; >390× speedup while maintaining image quality; validated on EFM (67× speedup); no hardware modifications required
comments: Generalizability across lock-in AFM techniques (PFM, EFM) demonstrated; transfer learning approach practical; speed-sensitivity trade-off fundamentally overcome via neural networks.

model_io.model: Sequential U-Net CNN for PFM/EFM image reconstruction
Transfer learning framework

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deep learning reconstruction enables >10× speedup in lock-in AFM without quality loss via neural image super-resolution

title: Demonstrating optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit
task: Demonstrate optical control of complex phases in trapped-ion qubits with decoherence resilience
key_results: Measured ground-state phases via optical driving to excited state using spectator level reference; geometric phases not inherently immune to decoherence; time-integrated excited-state population governs decoherence sensitivity (not phase type); implemented error-suppression strategies; four phase-imprinting protocols benchmarked under engineered dissipation
comments: Challenges geometric-phase robustness folklore; critical finding that decoherence depends on excitation dynamics not phase nature; practical error mitigation strategy demonstrated on 40Ca⁺.

model_io.model: 40Ca⁺ trapped-ion qubit with optical phase control

hypotheses.hypothesis: Geometric phases exhibit inherent robustness to systematic errors but not necessarily to decoherence; decoherence sensitivity governed by time-integrated excited-state population
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated geometric phases vulnerable to decoherence; phase type (geometric vs dynamical) less predictive of robustness than excitation time integral

title: Investigation of the guaiazulene–p-chloranil charge transfer complex in solution: a combined spectroscopic and quantum chemical approach
task: Characterize guaiazulene–p-chloranil donor-acceptor charge-transfer complex in solution
key_results: Binding constants from absorption (20,830 dm³ mol⁻¹) and fluorescence quenching (43,560 dm³ mol⁻¹); CT absorption band at 808 nm (1.537 eV experimental, 1.534 eV TDDFT); strong intermolecular coupling from π-system–π* orbital overlap; DFT/TDDFT excellently predict CT transition energy
comments: Excellent agreement between experimental absorption and TDDFT predictions validates computational methodology; binding constant disparity (fluorescence > absorption) suggests dynamic equilibrium complexity.

model_io.model: Guaiazulene–p-chloranil D–A complex in solution
DFT/TDDFT calculations (gas phase and non-polar solvent)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Strong intermolecular π-system–π* coupling enables stable D–A complex with CT transition energy accurately predicted by TDDFT
hypotheses.result: CT energy agreement (1.537 eV exp. vs 1.534 eV calc.); binding constants 20,830–43,560 dm³ mol⁻¹; favorable orbital alignment confirmed

title: Gas capture and selective sensing performance of graphene-like AlNC2 monolayer: a DFT study
task: Investigate gas adsorption and selective sensing on graphene-like AlNC2 monolayer
key_results: Strong chemisorption for NO₂, SO₂, NO, NH₃ (adsorption energies indicate stable binding); moderate interaction CO, H₂S; weak CH₄; reversible adsorption for moderately adsorbed species; difficult desorption for chemisorbed gases at ambient T
comments: DFT study demonstrates dual capability (capture + sensing); band-gap narrowing and new Fermi-level states confirm strong electronic interactions; AlNC2 stability confirmed by phonon spectrum.

model_io.model: AlNC2 graphene-like monolayer (DFT)
inputs: gas molecules (CO, NO, NO₂, SO₂, NH₃, H₂S, CH₄)

hypotheses.hypothesis: AlNC2 exhibits differential adsorption strengths enabling selective gas sensing with reversibility for weakly-bound species and capture for strongly-bound species
hypotheses.result: Strong chemisorption NO₂/SO₂/NO/NH₃; reversible moderate adsorption CO/H₂S; irreversible capture behavior at ambient T

title: Organ at risk sparing by non-coplanar prone breast radiotherapy on Halcyon/Ethos linacs utilizing breast couch slewing
task: Optimize non-coplanar prone-position breast radiotherapy with breast-couch slewing to reduce organ-at-risk dose
key_results: Non-coplanar short-arc VMAT with ±15–20° angular separation reduces mean dose to heart/lungs/esophagus by >20% vs coplanar; ±15° achieves best compromise between OAR sparing and technical feasibility; prone crawl position with couch slewing up to 20° (transverse) is technically feasible
comments: Practical optimization balances dose reduction with linac constraints (couch rotation limitations); prone + DIBH + non-coplanar triple-approach addresses adjuvant breast/axillary/periclavicular coverage; planning study but no clinical outcomes reported.

model_io.model: Non-coplanar short-arc VMAT radiotherapy plan on Halcyon/Ethos linacs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-coplanar techniques with ±15–20° angular separation and couch slewing reduce OAR dose without prohibitive technical complexity
hypotheses.result: >20% mean-dose reduction to heart/lungs/esophagus; ±15° identified as optimal compromise

title: Impedance study of the charge leakage phenomenon in ITO-free graphene-super-yellow light-emitting diode
task: Analyze charge leakage and interface transport in ITO-free graphene/MoO₃/polymer light-emitting diode
key_results: Increased hole injection relative to electron injection; significant hole-electron recombination at graphene-polymer interface causes charge leakage; impedance spectroscopy and equivalent circuit modeling reveal charge density and leakage mechanisms; novel mathematical model interprets interface electronic processes
comments: Impedance spectroscopy methodology effectively decouples charge transport phenomena; graphene/MoO₃ anode shows promise for ITO replacement but interface engineering critical to minimize leakage.

model_io.model: OLED with graphene/MoO₃ anode and poly(para-phenylene vinylene) emitting layer
Impedance spectroscopy measurement and equivalent circuit model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Graphene/MoO₃/polymer interface exhibits hole-dominated charge transport with significant recombination-induced leakage
hypotheses.result: Impedance analysis revealed increased hole injection and charge leakage at graphene-polymer junction

title: Broadband solar energy harvesting and near-perfect thermal emission on a unified stepped-high concentric dual-ring metamaterial
task: Develop broadband solar absorber using titanium-nitride-based metamaterial for energy harvesting and thermal emission
key_results: 99.27% absorptivity 150–3000 nm; stepped-height concentric dual-ring design with TiN; near-ideal blackbody emission 373–1500 K; angular independence up to 60°; superior to noble-metal designs in thermal stability
comments: Outstanding multi-resonance coupling and impedance matching across ultra-broadband spectrum; TiN refractory properties address stability limitations of conventional designs.

model_io.model: Stepped-height concentric dual-ring metamaterial absorber (SHCDR-MA) on TiN/SiO2 substrate

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vertical impedance gradient and multi-resonance coupling (interband transitions, surface plasmons, guided modes) enable broadband absorption with TiN stability
hypotheses.result: Achieved 99.27% absorptivity across 150–3000 nm with temperature-invariant blackbody emission

task: Design multifunctional anisotropic photonic crystal with Tamm plasmon mode for sensing, filtering, and polarization control
